verdict: GE HealthCare grew revenue 7% to $5.5B and profit attributable to shareholders 38% to $615M, with pharmaceutical diagnostics up 13% and imaging up 6%.

segments.name: Advanced Imaging Solutions
segments.note: CT, MR, X-ray, ultrasound and image-guided therapy systems — the largest business, growing 6.1% (4.5% organically).

segments.name: Pharmaceutical Diagnostics
segments.note: Contrast agents and radiopharmaceuticals used in imaging — the fastest-growing segment at +13.0%.

segments.name: Patient Care Solutions
segments.note: Patient monitoring and related care technology — up 8.5% (reported as $793M; shown $1M higher so segments foot to total revenue).

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: Selling, general and administrative costs (reported as $1,100M; shown $1M lower so the lines foot exactly to reported operating income).

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Developing imaging, monitoring and diagnostics technology.

otherDetail: Interest and other financial charges of $122M, partly offset by $50M of non-operating benefit-plan income and $19M of other income — a net $53M drag.
footerNote: Net income in the chart is the total of $623M; $615M was attributable to GE HealthCare shareholders. Cost of revenue is cost of products ($2,373M) plus cost of services ($916M).

takeaways.title: Diagnostics led growth
takeaways.text: Pharmaceutical Diagnostics grew 13.0% (13.8% organically) at a 29.9% segment EBIT margin — the most profitable business — while the big imaging segment grew 6.1%.

takeaways.title: EPS jumped 39%
takeaways.text: Diluted EPS of $1.36 rose $0.38 year over year as operating income grew 23% to $805M and the tax bill fell; adjusted EPS was $1.34.

takeaways.title: Orders kept pace
takeaways.text: Orders grew 4.0% organically with a book-to-bill of 1.03 and a $23.7B backlog — demand is healthy, if not booming, across hospital capital budgets.
